steps.title: Python & SQL Foundations
steps.subtitle: Write the code every pipeline runs on
steps.description: Data engineering is built on two languages: Python to move and reshape data, and SQL to query it. Learn to process files efficiently (CSV, JSON, Parquet), write advanced SQL with window functions, and understand how indexes and transactions keep databases fast and correct.

topics.name: Python for data: lists, dicts, sets, comprehensions, functions and exception handling
Processing large files with iterators and generators, plus the csv and json modules
File formats: CSV vs JSON vs Parquet (row vs columnar, schema, compression) with pandas/PyArrow
SQL core: SELECT, WHERE, JOINs, GROUP BY/HAVING and NULL handling
Advanced SQL: subqueries, CTEs and window functions (ROW_NUMBER, RANK, LAG) for deduplication and running totals
Keys and indexes: primary/foreign keys, B-tree and composite indexes, reading EXPLAIN plans
Transactions: ACID, isolation levels and upserts (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT / MERGE)

steps.title: Data Modeling & Warehousing
steps.subtitle: Design tables that analytics can trust
steps.description: Learn how analytical databases differ from application databases and how to model data for them: normalization vs denormalization, star and snowflake schemas, fact grain and slowly changing dimensions. You also see how columnar cloud warehouses such as Snowflake, BigQuery and Redshift store your data and charge for your queries.

topics.name: OLTP vs OLAP workloads and why analytics runs in a separate warehouse
Normalization (1NF to 3NF) vs denormalization and their trade-offs
Dimensional modeling: facts and measures (additive vs semi-additive), dimensions, grain, surrogate keys and conformed dimensions
Star vs snowflake schemas: design a sales data mart end to end
Slowly changing dimensions: Type 1, Type 2 (valid_from/valid_to, is_current), Type 3 and point-in-time joins
Columnar storage, compression, partitioning and clustering/sort keys
Cloud warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift): storage/compute separation and cost-aware queries

steps.title: ETL/ELT Pipelines & Orchestration
steps.subtitle: Move data reliably, on schedule
steps.description: Build batch pipelines that can be re-run safely: idempotent and incremental loads, change data capture and backfills. Orchestrate them with Apache Airflow, transform and test data with dbt, and add data quality checks so bad data never reaches a dashboard.

topics.name: ETL vs ELT and layered batch pipelines (raw, staging, marts)
Idempotent, re-runnable loads: partition overwrite, MERGE/upsert and safe backfills
Incremental loads with high-water marks, and log-based change data capture (CDC) with Debezium
Apache Airflow: DAGs, operators, dependencies, schedules, data intervals, retries and catchup
dbt: models, ref() and sources, materializations (view, table, incremental) and data tests
Data quality checks: not-null, uniqueness, referential integrity, volume and freshness
Failure handling: retries, alerting, SLAs and quarantining bad records

steps.title: Big Data & Streaming
steps.subtitle: Process data at scale, in batch and in real time
steps.description: Scale out with Apache Spark: DataFrames, lazy evaluation, partitioning, shuffles and join strategies. Then move to real-time data with Kafka topics, partitions and consumer groups, and stream-processing ideas such as windows, watermarks and exactly-once semantics.

topics.name: Spark architecture: driver, executors, lazy transformations vs actions, jobs, stages and tasks
PySpark DataFrames and Spark SQL: select, filter, groupBy, joins and built-in functions vs UDFs
Partitions and shuffles: repartition vs coalesce, broadcast joins, data skew and AQE
Kafka fundamentals: brokers, topics, partitions, offsets, replication and retention
Kafka producers and consumer groups: message keys and ordering, partition assignment, offset commits and lag
Stream processing: event time vs processing time, tumbling/sliding/session windows and watermarks
Delivery guarantees: at-most-once, at-least-once and exactly-once with checkpoints and idempotent sinks

steps.title: Cloud Data Platforms & DataOps
steps.subtitle: Run production data platforms in the cloud
steps.description: Put it all together on a modern cloud platform: data lakes and lakehouses built with Delta Lake or Apache Iceberg on object storage, Docker and CI/CD for pipelines, and the monitoring, lineage, governance and security practices that keep production data reliable and compliant.

topics.name: Data lake vs warehouse vs lakehouse, and the medallion (bronze/silver/gold) architecture
Open table formats: Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg (ACID commits, time travel and VACUUM retention, schema evolution, compaction)
Cloud object storage (Amazon S3, GCS, ADLS): partition layout, file sizing and query engines such as Athena
Docker for pipelines and CI/CD for data: Git workflow, automated dbt builds and tests on pull requests
Data observability: freshness and volume monitoring, alerting and data lineage
Governance and security: IAM least privilege, secrets management, encryption and PII masking
Cost control: partition and column pruning, auto-suspending compute and storage lifecycle rules
